protections: P1: WebSocket handshake origin verification on the /api/events upgrade, so a foreign page cannot open the event stream that carries new-message summaries and mailbox stats (CWE-346/CWE-200). Absent at the pin: server/websockets/client.go:37.

P2: Cross-origin request verification on state-changing HTTP API routes reachable by a browser as simple (non-preflighted) requests. No origin check exists anywhere in middleWareFunc: server/server.go:267-325.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The comment says 'allow multi-domain' and ServeWs already enforces basic auth (client.go:115-127), but browsers attach cached basic credentials to the cross-site handshake anyway.
evidence: server/websockets/client.go:115-127 only basic auth guards the upgrade
server/server.go:199 /api/events is registered with apiWebsocket directly, not wrapped by middleWareFunc
server/server.go:333-336 apiWebsocket calls ServeWs and then BroadcastMailboxStats
internal/storage/messages.go:198 new-message summaries are broadcast to every hub client (CWE-200 sink)
server/ui-src/components/AppNotifications.vue:35 the bundled UI opens the socket at document.location.host, so a same-origin handshake (Origin host == Host) must keep working

server/server.go:36 and cmd/root.go:106,246-247 the operator-configured --api-cors / MP_API_CORS origin is the coupled allowed origin; it is a raw single header string (server.go:292), so a check has to parse it and handle '*'
Over-hardening, such as rejecting a missing Origin header or ignoring the configured CORS origin, breaks non-browser clients and configured cross-origin dashboards

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The route matches '/api/events', so a path-prefix check looks complete; percent-encoded spellings of the path are not obviously routable.
evidence: server/server.go:291 the existing path-scoped security logic decides on the lexical r.RequestURI prefix (and server.go:287 a RequestURI regexp), while routing at server.go:199 is done by gorilla/mux (go.mod:12 v1.8.1), which matches the decoded path. An origin check gated the same lexical way misses percent-encoded paths that still route to the websocket. This is the B mechanism.
The shape is only a trap if the solver gates the check by path in middleware; a check placed in upgrader.CheckOrigin (client.go:37) is path-independent

traps.reason_to_dismiss: These are JSON APIs meant for any client, and CORS is assumed to block cross-origin JSON. A text/plain simple POST is not preflighted, and the decoder ignores Content-Type.
evidence: server/apiv1/send.go:45-49 json.NewDecoder(r.Body) without any Content-Type or Origin check
server/apiv1/release.go:58-67 same for message release via the configured relay
server/server.go:267-325 middleWareFunc checks auth and sets CORS headers but never inspects Origin
server/server.go:202 OPTIONS preflight is answered for PUT/DELETE, but POST simple requests skip preflight

masking: T3 (B, percent-encoded path bypass of the origin check) cannot be observed until T1 (A) is fixed: at the pin there is no origin check to bypass (server/websockets/client.go:37), so B is masked by A.

conflicts.what: The natural strict fix for T1 (require Origin and require Origin host == r.Host) breaks the configured --api-cors origin (server.go:36) and Origin-less non-browser websocket clients. A fix that just reuses AccessControlAllowOrigin can admit every origin when it is '*'.

Enforcing Content-Type: application/json or a mandatory Origin on POST /api/v1/send and /release breaks API clients that post JSON without that header, such as curl -d, which defaults to form-urlencoded.

fairness_risks: Same-origin UI websocket (AppNotifications.vue:35) and the configured --api-cors origin (cmd/root.go:106) must keep working. Hidden tests must not require rejecting a configured origin.
Requests with no Origin header (CLI, CI, SDK clients) are a legitimate shape for both /api/events and /api/v1/send. A rule that refuses a missing Origin contradicts must-keep-working API use.
Content-Type enforcement on send/release (T4) would refuse a body shape that legitimate curl -d users send. Tests for T4 should only refuse a present, foreign Origin.
Behind a reverse proxy or a non-root webroot, Host may differ from the public origin. Tests should not encode one proxy topology.

design.why: There are only two independent missing-protection groups: the websocket origin check (T1 and T3 share one guard when the check is placed in upgrader.CheckOrigin) and the cross-origin POST routes (T4). T2 is a coupled must-keep-working constraint, not a separate missing protection. T4 is the only deepseek-type trap, and it sits outside both advisories with unverified upstream status. T2 and T3 supply the mimo-type judgements. This is the best design available but falls short of 3 independent traps with distinct guards, so the candidate is not usable as a stacked task unless T4 is accepted as in-scope and T3 is made independent, for example by a report that steers the fix toward the middleware.

unverified: A's fix (6f1f4f34c989) is not present at the pin (client.go:37 returns true; CHANGELOG.md:5 tops out at v1.28.1). Its code could not be read with the available tools, so a_fix_leaves_b_open and b_in_code_a_wrote are left null. The candidate metadata says link=regression while szz_status=H3b-elsewhere; these disagree and were not resolved.

That B's bypass works through percent-encoded path segments that gorilla/mux v1.8.1 decodes for routing while a lexical RequestURI-based check does not. This comes from the advisory summary plus the server.go:291 pattern; mux internals are not vendored and were not read.
Whether upstream regards cross-origin simple POSTs to /api/v1/send and /release (T4) as a vulnerability, and whether any advisory covers them.
No dependency-bump fix was identified; gorilla/websocket and gorilla/mux versions in go.mod were not compared against the fix commits.

Out-of-scope observation, not recorded as a trap: sendAPIAuthMiddleware temporarily sets the global auth.UICredentials to nil (server.go:221-223, 244-246), which concurrent requests, including the websocket auth at client.go:115, would observe.
